---
title: "Proposed content overview"
---

## Chemical foundations

Follow a substance through environmental compartments. Practise concentration
units, mass balances, and the distinction between equilibrium and reaction rate.

## Atmosphere

Explain ozone formation and removal, photochemical pollution, acid deposition,
and the chemical roles of gases and particles in climate. Follow deposition
into surface waters.

## Water

Use acid–base equilibria, carbonate buffering, and gas exchange to explain water
composition. The first draft of [carbonate and gas chemistry](carbonate-gases/notes.qmd)
includes lectures and practice. Relate organic matter, redox conditions, metal complexation, and
surface reactions to speciation and mobility. Apply these ideas to nutrient
cycling and water treatment.

## Soils and contaminants

Explain retention and release in soils and sediments. Connect organic molecular
properties to partitioning, persistence, and potential exposure. Use waste and
leachate as applications of the same chemistry.

## Connecting the systems

Trace acid deposition through a catchment to a lake, or explain contaminant
release when sediment conditions change. Support an explanation with reactions,
a mass balance, and a clearly interpreted figure.

## Working reference

Gary W. vanLoon and Stephen J. Duffy, *Environmental Chemistry: A Global
Perspective*, fourth edition, Oxford University Press, 2017,
ISBN 9780198749974. Selected readings will follow the
[publisher's chapter structure](https://www.oup.com.au/books/higher-education/chemistry/9780198749974).
This is the working reference for content development; assignment to this course
is provisional.
